paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. When the hardest hour of His life came, Jesus went to prayer. He said, "Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours be done." (Luke 22:42) He asked honestly for what He wanted, and then He trusted His Father with the answer.

Now look at everybody else in that garden. The disciples were asleep, exhausted from sorrow (Luke 22:45), and Jesus told them twice to pray so they would not enter into temptation (Luke 22:40, 46). I have dozed off on oven duty, so I'm not throwing stones. But the lesson is simple: when you're worn out and the pressure is rising, prayer is the thing to reach for first, not the last thing you try.

And see how Jesus carries Himself when the crowd shows up. A friend's kiss turns into a betrayal, a sword swings, and Jesus says, "No more of this!" and heals the servant's ear (Luke 22:51). He tells them, "this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness." (Luke 22:53) Friend, even in the dark hour, He stays calm, stays kind and stays on the path of His Father's will, and that is the kind of baker we're all learning to be.
